chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to me, he said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever cuts out a new garment and recites 'Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree' (Surah al-Qadr) thirty-six times, and when he reaches 'the angels descend,' he takes out some water and sprinkles some of it lightly upon the garment,

then prays two units of prayer wearing it and supplicates to his Lord, saying in his supplication: 'Praise be to God who has provided me with that which beautifies me among the people, covers my nakedness, and in which I pray to my Lord,'
and praises God — he will continue to eat in abundance until that garment wears out.

key_terms.إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر: Surah al-Qadr (Chapter 97), recited as part of this practice

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when wearing new clothes in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches a practice for blessing a new garment: reciting Surah al-Qadr thirty-six times while cutting the cloth, sprinkling it with water at a specific verse, praying two units of prayer in it, and reciting a supplication of gratitude for clothing. The reward is continued sustenance and abundance for as long as the garment lasts. This teaching reflects the Islamic principle of connecting daily activities like acquiring new clothing with acts of worship and gratitude to God.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
